text: Needs meaningful chances to experience competence rather than constant adult rescue.
Needs predictable routines that reduce unnecessary cognitive load.
Needs adults who separate mistakes from character.
Needs specific feedback about strategies, effort, and next steps.
Needs enough sleep to support attention, learning, mood, and physical wellbeing.
Needs regular opportunities for active movement and skill-building.
Needs unhurried time for play, hobbies, and self-directed interests.
Needs adults to listen seriously when peer problems matter to them.
Needs manageable responsibilities that genuinely contribute to family life.
Needs challenges that are difficult enough to require practice but not so large that they feel impossible.
Needs permission to ask for help without losing ownership of the task.
Needs opportunities to make choices within clear boundaries.
Needs access to books and conversation that stretch language and knowledge.
Needs adults who model how to change strategies when the first approach fails.
Needs practice resolving ordinary conflicts rather than having every conflict solved for them.
Needs balanced opportunities for competition and cooperation.
Needs digital boundaries that protect sleep, schoolwork, relationships, movement, and other interests.
Needs food routines that provide variety without turning eating into a moral contest.
Needs opportunities to see adults learning, practicing, apologizing, and trying again.
Needs time to develop interests without every interest becoming a performance goal.
Needs clear expectations about belongings, chores, homework, and shared spaces.
Needs encouragement to notice progress that may be invisible day to day.
Needs room for both achievement and ordinary silliness.
Needs trusted adults who remain available as independence grows.
Needs a family culture where asking questions is treated as a strength.
